transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. I'm here to help you. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Honestly, Dr. Smith, for the past year I've been feeling absolutely on top of the world with this incredible, overflowing energy to do absolutely everything! But at the same time, I find myself getting extremely irritated and snapping at people over the tiniest little things. It's like my mind and body are constantly running at a hundred miles an hour and I'm just so incredibly driven!

During these high-energy periods, have you ever experienced symptoms severe enough to require hospitalization, or have you had a period where your behavior was so extreme that it caused significant problems at work or in your personal relationships?

I've never been hospitalized, but my behavior has definitely caused some major problems for me and my family. I've gone on these reckless, unrestrained buying sprees that put us in serious financial distress, and I even made some rash business investments without properly reviewing them first.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were [Bipolar I Disorder, Bipolar II Disorder]. The patient reports reckless behavior (financial distress and rash business investments) that caused significant problems in their personal life and work, which aligns more closely with the criteria for a manic episode rather than a hypomanic episode, pointing toward Bipolar I Disorder.
